title: Walmart - Production of competitive advantage.
peek: Walmart shows how a market without barriers can be turned to one with barriers through a system of mutually reinforcing activities.
pain:
Walmart entered what looked like a fish market: undifferentiated products, price-sensitive customers and theoretically low barriers to imitation. It won by making low prices a system rather than a tactic. Scale lowered procurement and distribution costs; dense store networks lowered logistics costs; high inventory velocity lowered capital requirements; EDLP reduced promotional complexity; the resulting prices increased volume, which further strengthened Walmart's scale.

The moat was not a single barrier to entry. The moat was the interaction between many small advantages that became extremely difficult to reproduce simultaneously.
